title: matplotlib: a bar chart, captured at the end
source:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

harvest = {}
for crop, kg in zip(["maize", "beans", "wheat", "sorghum"], [1840, 920, 1310, 760]):
    harvest[crop] = kg

plt.bar(list(harvest), list(harvest.values()), color="tab:orange")
plt.title("Harvest by crop")
plt.ylabel("Harvest (kg)")
print("Total:", sum(harvest.values()), "kg")

steps.narration: harvest now refers to a new dict.
Iteration 1 of the for loop: crop is now 'maize' and kg is now 1840.
Added the key 'maize' to harvest, with the value 1840.
Iteration 2 of the for loop: crop is now 'beans' and kg is now 920.
Added the key 'beans' to harvest, with the value 920.
Iteration 3 of the for loop: crop is now 'wheat' and kg is now 1310.
Added the key 'wheat' to harvest, with the value 1310.
Iteration 4 of the for loop: crop is now 'sorghum' and kg is now 760.
Added the key 'sorghum' to harvest, with the value 760.
The for loop ends after 4 iterations.
Drew a bar chart on the current axes: one bar for each item of list(harvest), its height from list(harvest.values()).
Set the title of the current axes to "Harvest by crop".
Set the y-axis label of the current axes to "Harvest (kg)".
Figure 1 was still open when the program ended, so it is in the output too: a bar chart titled Harvest by crop, with the y axis labelled Harvest (kg).
